picks.title: Chatbot Intervention and Cancer Risk Knowledge in Adolescents and Young Adults With Cancer Predisposition
picks.excerpt: A randomized clinical trial tested an electronic chatbot-based cancer risk communication tool for adolescents and young adults with hereditary cancer predisposition syndromes.
picks.rationale: Randomized trial of a patient-facing chatbot for young people with hereditary cancer syndromes: RCT-level evidence on AI in genetic risk counseling.

picks.title: Inferring clinically relevant molecular subtypes of pancreatic cancer from routine histopathology using deep learning
picks.excerpt: Deep learning infers pancreatic cancer molecular subtypes, normally requiring costly gene-expression testing, directly from routine H&E histopathology slides.
picks.rationale: Reads treatment-relevant pancreatic cancer subtypes off routine H&E slides, which could stand in for costly gene-expression testing.

picks.title: Radiology AI authorizations rise 42% as regulatory landscape evolves
picks.excerpt: A new analysis of the FDA AI-enabled medical device database details how radiology AI authorizations rose 42% and how the regulatory standing of the technology has shifted.
picks.rationale: Analysis of the FDA AI-device database shows how fast cleared radiology AI is growing, the clearest picture of regulatory momentum.

picks.title: HHS announces new efforts to speed up, expand clinical trials with AI
picks.excerpt: HHS and ARPA-H announced new AI-driven efforts to speed up and expand clinical trials as federal officials seek to compete with countries like China.
picks.rationale: An official HHS/ARPA-H program announcement putting federal AI into trial design and recruitment, a concrete government action.

picks.title: A Precedent for Regulating Clinical AI Models
picks.excerpt: Former FDA commissioner Scott Gottlieb argues clinical AI models already in use could be regulated by improving on the pathway used for laboratory developed tests.
picks.rationale: A former FDA commissioner proposes a concrete route for regulating clinical AI models already in use, modeled on the lab-developed-test pathway. Aimed at regulators and health systems.

dedup.note: No candidate repeats a story in the 30-day history_digest, and the pool had no clusters. The only history_match was the JAMA Netw Open AYA chatbot RCT (band 'related' to the Clairity/Everlywell DTC breast-risk tool). It was checked and is a different story: a randomized trial of a counseling chatbot for hereditary syndromes, not a commercial access expansion. The 42% radiology AI analysis and the Gottlieb LDT-pathway proposal are distinct from the published FDA FY2027 guidance agenda: one is a database analysis, the other a policy proposal, and neither covers the CDRH agenda. Not picked: the STAT Anthropic/ARPA-H item (a newsletter segment, overlaps the ARPA-H trials story we picked), the npj pathology AI evidence-availability study (same regulatory theme as the 42% card), npj sepsis ICU-stay model (retrospective prediction, weaker), JAMA Pediatrics governance Viewpoint (generic), RB physician pushback on RFK Jr. (reaction piece), RB RSNA certificate (an education product update), STAT physician op-ed and Healthcare Dive insurer-vs-billing (commentary on cost research), Healthcare Dive privacy survey, MedCity cognitive-decline opinion, Fierce weekly rundown (a mixed roundup), and AuntMinnie ClearRead/RapidAI, CARPL/HOPPR and Oncosoft ASTRO (vendor integration or showcase pieces). Diversity: jamanetwork 2, nature.com 1, radiologybusiness 1, statnews 1, for 4 distinct outlets. No pick involves biosecurity or gain-of-function.
